policy.a_do_not_retry_unchanged_lesson_blocks: a mutation whose blocked_traits are all reproduced by the child genome, unless the child is tagged RETRY_WITH_CHANGED_CONDITION and names the changed condition
policy.retain_as_baseline_lessons_pin: the named seed candidates stay in the population for the whole search

lessons.title: The headline HML advantage was a prompt-envelope artifact
lessons.requirement: non-state prompt bytes must be byte-identical across arms

lessons.title: Prior HML syntax is not privileged among reasonable surfaces
Most measured accuracy was lexical
Serializer asymmetry can dominate the representation effect
Goal-centred ordering worsens locality
lessons.mechanism: relevance and dependency proximity are different relations
lessons.changed_condition_permitting_one_retry: the V2 runtime corpus carries real local contexts and reference edges; the prior corpus averaged 1.00 claims and zero dependencies

Flat S-expressions destroy record-order error detection
lessons.requirement: error detection is reported per mutation family and never averaged before selection

lessons.title: Compression is a diagnostic, never the objective
lessons.requirement: token count is a Pareto axis, never a scalar objective

lessons.title: The line-based locality metric was an artifact
lessons.requirement: distances are measured in characters and tokens; lines are never a distance unit

lessons.title: The minimal-pair instrument saturated

An opaque wrapper is not a semantic state
Derived structured projections were lossy where it mattered
lessons.requirement: the search reads elaborated Lean runtime identities, never a re-parse of pretty text

lessons.title: Real corpora can be too structurally trivial to discriminate
lessons.requirement: structural-richness statistics accompany every locality result

lessons.title: Trace provenance is not fresh replay
Generic structured representations sometimes matched or beat HML
lessons.note: stated in the mission brief; the only local measurement supporting it is FM-002's Stage-1 table. Not cited as an independent result.

lessons.title: Excessive compression is not automatically beneficial
lessons.note: held as a design principle and enforced by the Pareto vector; no local experiment measured a compression-induced accuracy loss.

lessons.title: Glyph token cost is a property of the vocabulary, not of the representation
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, pinned GPT-2 byte-level BPE
lessons.note: FM-004's escaping penalty reproduces under a second, independent vocabulary, so the UTF-8 hard gate is not an artifact of one tokenizer. The absolute token counts do not reproduce: every glyph the corpus needs is one token under Qwen3-8B and two or three under GPT-2. Any absolute token ranking is a statement about a vocabulary.
lessons.requirement: report token counts alongside bytes and tokenizer-free pre-tokens, and name the vocabulary in every token claim

lessons.title: Identifier-corruption detection saturates across every candidate
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, generation-zero seeds, 24 real V2 transitions
lessons.note: An altered identifier either fails to resolve or resolves to a different declaration, so every representation over an identity-carrying canonical state detects it. The axis was removed from Pareto selection before the search began and detect_drop_field took its place. detect_truncate_tail reads 0.000 for fifteen of sixteen seeds because the trailing block is usually the structured delta, which is outside the declared semantic contract; the one exception drops the delta entirely, which makes its tail contract content.
lessons.requirement: an instrument whose arms all saturate is reported as non-discriminative and excluded from selection, never reported as agreement

lessons.title: Goal linearization is unmeasurable on a corpus of single-goal states
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, pilot run, 317-transition V2 corpus
lessons.note: This is FM-014's problem in a new place and now quantified per axis. The V2 corpus is structurally rich in local context (mean 13.4 declarations, 63.4 intra-context references) so context_order moves the measurement 90% of the time, but it averages 1.01 goals per state, so every goal-linearization strategy renders identically. A ranking over graph_serialization from this corpus would be selection on noise.
lessons.requirement: report the share of single-axis mutations that changed the measurement, per axis, beside any claim about that axis; an axis at 0% is reported as unmeasurable on this corpus rather than as tied

lessons.title: Goal-centred ordering loses again, now on a corpus that has real dependencies
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, pilot run, 317-transition V2 corpus
lessons.note: FM-005 allowed exactly one retry on the stated changed condition that the V2 corpus carries real local-context dependency structure, unlike the prior corpus with 1.00 claims and zero dependencies. The retry was taken and the result reproduced: grouping declarations by relevance to the goal made binder-use distance worse, not better. The mechanism FM-005 named -- relevance and dependency proximity are different relations -- now has support from a corpus averaging 13.4 local declarations and 63.4 intra-context references.

lessons.title: Hoisting shared subterms into a DAG more than doubles token cost
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, pilot run, 317-transition V2 corpus
lessons.note: The intuition is that a subterm repeated n times should be written once. Measured, the alias table plus the reference machinery costs far more than the sharing saves on real Lean expression trees: elaborated subterms that repeat are mostly small, and the ones large enough to be worth hoisting are rarely repeated. It also halved record-order corruption detection, because an alias section separates a record from the content that identifies it.
lessons.changed_condition_permitting_one_retry: a corpus whose expression trees repeat large maximal subterms -- measure the repeat-size distribution before retrying

lessons.title: Naive substring matching inflated the locality metric
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, found while the definitive run was in progress
lessons.note: Short identity tokens are prefixes of longer ones. Searching for 'bf1' with a plain substring scan also matched inside 'bf10'..'bf19', overcounting mentions by 25% on the first transition checked and distorting every distance derived from them. Premise names had the same defect: 'Nat.add' matches inside 'Nat.add_comm'. Fixed by requiring a non-word character on both sides. The pilot run's locality figures were computed before this fix and are inflated; the definitive run is not comparable to them and the pilot's numbers are retained only as archived history.
lessons.requirement: identity and premise occurrences are counted with token boundaries, never with a plain substring scan

lessons.title: Cost and locality rank stably; corruption detection does not
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, finalists measured on SEARCH_DEV and on the never-selected SEARCH_VALIDATION split, and separately across 16+ Mathlib domains
lessons.note: Two independent checks agree. Across a held-out split selection never read, the cost and locality axes rank the finalists almost identically (rho 0.93-1.00) while record-swap detection nearly loses its ordering (rho 0.357). Across Mathlib domains, the same three axes have one leader in 100% of domains while the detection axes have a modal leader in only 56-69%. Cost and locality are properties of the representation; corruption detection depends on what the state happens to contain.
lessons.requirement: a corruption-detection claim names its sample and is reported with its cross-split rank correlation; a cost or locality claim may be stated for the representation

lessons.title: A colon heuristic made four of nine microtest suites read 100% unanswerable
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 open-ended search V2, while building the structural-access suites
lessons.note: The suites decided whether to route an identity through the candidate's identity codec by testing whether the identity contained a colon. That was a guess about the shape of canonical identities, and it was wrong: the committed corpus uses short identities such as m9 and f17, so the test was false and the suite searched a rendering containing 'bm9' for the string 'm9'. Every identity now routes through the codec unconditionally, which returns unknown names unchanged and is therefore correct for both canonical identities and global constants like Nat.add. A second defect in the same family: the delta suite counted a goal identity found anywhere in the rendering as answering 'which goals did this step solve?', so a representation that omits the delta scored as if it stated it; relational queries are now scoped to the section that states the relation.
lessons.requirement: an instrument is checked against a real rendering before any number it produces is reported; a rate over zero queries is reported as zero queries, never as agreement

lessons.title: An invented axis can be accepted, registered, and completely inert
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 open-ended search V2, first live generation
lessons.note: In the first live generation the model-driven meta-designer proposed three new axes with plausible mechanisms -- goal_refinement, context_signature, context_range -- and all three were accepted, registered, and bumped the genome schema to v2.3.0. All nine of their axis-value combinations then rendered IDENTICALLY. Two causes, both mine. First, the projection hooks matched value names literally ('GOAL_LOCAL', 'BEFORE'), so an axis whose inventor chose WIDE/NARROW took a fallback branch that happened to reproduce the existing layout; hooks now index behaviour by the value's position among the non-NONE values, so any naming works. Second, acceptance condition 6 -- 'at least one value differs observably on the corpus' -- was written in the spec and never enforced; registration now renders every value on a sample and rejects the axis as NO_OBSERVABLE_EFFECT if they all agree.
lessons.requirement: an invented axis is provisionally registered, then rendered at every value on a sample, and kept only if at least two values differ; an inert axis is worse than no axis because it consumes search budget and inflates the apparent size of the space

lessons.title: The validation gate mislabelled consistently-worse candidates as non-generalizing
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 open-ended search V2, generation 1, seen in the live verdict stream
lessons.note: A child whose target metric got 2.2% worse on dev and 2.1% worse on validation was labelled NON_GENERALIZING_MUTATION and blocked from the elite population. Dev and validation agreed almost exactly; there was no dev-set claim for validation to fail to reproduce. The gate's job is specifically to catch improvements that exist only on dev, so a candidate that failed on both is a failed hypothesis and belongs to Pareto selection, which may still keep it for being best on a different axis. Blocking it let the validation gate silently override the selector.
lessons.requirement: the validation gate blocks eliteness only when a positive dev gain fails to reproduce; a hypothesis that failed on both splits is recorded as HYPOTHESIS_FAILED_CONSISTENTLY and left to the Pareto selector
